name: Feature-Flagged Canary Experiment
phase: Metrics, Telemetry, and Innovation Accounting Tactics
hypothesis: We believe that [Redesigned Workflow X] increases task completion rates compared to the current baseline. We will verify this by deploying the redesign to 10% of production traffic via an open-source feature flag, and consider it validated if the treatment group shows a statistically significant lift in task completions (≥ 15%, p < 0.05) without degrading error rates or latency.
schematic: Split at step 2 of the 3-step strip

plan.label: Preparation
plan.text: Put the new workflow behind a feature flag with exposure keys and logging attributes.

plan.label: Execution
plan.text: Split 10% of traffic at random, watch errors, then raise to 50% once it is stable.

plan.label: Data collection
plan.text: Compare conversion, errors, latency and completion time between control and treatment.

planFull.label: Preparation
planFull.text: Instrument the alternative workflow behind a dynamic feature flag rule, defining exposure keys and logging attributes.

planFull.label: Execution
planFull.text: Route a randomized 10% traffic split to the variant while monitoring error logs and system health. Gradually increase traffic to 50% as system stability is confirmed.

planFull.label: Data collection
planFull.text: Track conversion rates, system errors, operational latency, and task completion times across both control and treatment variations.

warning.label: Early Peeking and Underpowered Samples
warning.text: Stopping when p dips below 0.05 inflates false positives; lock sample size and duration first.

warningFull: Stopping an experiment early the moment a p-value dips below 0.05 dramatically increases the rate of false positives; sample sizes and experiment durations must be locked in advance.
